recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if CQI later adopts different normative guidance for partial MeasureReport responses or bulk-data-based quality measurement at scale.
issue_request: FHIR-16811 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the STU3 MeasureReport guidance. It asked what to do when a subject-list MeasureReport would need thousands of references to individual-level reports for very large populations, and the approved resolution was to document that implementations can impose an upper limit and only report summary-level information after that point.
initial_application: Git commit b1633598ee8a1c6256a166a585b3a96af299c644, matching the Jira comment for SVN 14853, applied GF#16811 by adding a large-population note to source/clinicalreasoning-quality-reporting.html. The note said implementations may limit the result size with a too-costly error or a partial response marked as partial, and referenced bulk data feedback.
additional_context: The current source location is in build scope: source/hierarchy.xml lists clinicalreasoning-quality-reporting.html and source/fhir.ini lists MeasureReport as an active resource. Later commits changed patient language to subject language and adapted the paragraph to cover both subjectResults and subjectReport paths without removing the large-population rule. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current Subject-List Reports section in source/clinicalreasoning-quality-reporting.html already includes the requested guidance for very large populations.

related_jiras.note: A same-day source-history commit changed the same Quality Reporting section from patient wording to subject wording while preserving the FHIR-16811 large-population guidance.
A later source-history commit refactored the Subject-List Reports text to cover both subjectResults and subjectReport paths while retaining the FHIR-16811 guidance.
